personality: It speaks in procedure and yet means wound. Every declaration it issues arrives with the quality of something already decided before the question was asked. It does not conceal this — it simply does not consider it a problem worth addressing.
garment: A heavy institutional robe of boiled charcoal wool, split asymmetrically at the hem as though torn and re-hemmed many times, bound at the waist with a doubled leather strap bearing stamped registry marks, the left shoulder bearing a sewn patch of darker cloth that does not match — older, stiffer, from another garment entirely.
prop: A cleaving iron — short-handled, broad-bladed, edge notched from repeated use — held loosely at the side, neither threatening nor sheathed, simply present.
detail: The right hand's knuckles are wrapped in linen strips, wound in the manner of official record-binding, some strips bearing faint stamped numerals.
mood: The face holds no expression that resolves — features arranged in the posture of focus but the eyes track something slightly beside the person in front of them, as though reading text superimposed on the air.
posture: Weight planted, torso slightly forward, one foot ahead of the other — the stance of someone mid-step who has decided to stop and will not explain why.
body_type: Broad through the shoulders, built for sustained force rather than speed, carrying the density of someone who has absorbed many decisions without softening.
age: Late forties — an age that reads not as lived but as accumulated, the way institutional residue accumulates in corners.
era_blend: Carries a waterwheel registry seal on a chain at the belt — a mechanical device for stamping severance documents, spring-loaded, crude, always primed — the only concession to mechanism on an otherwise entirely procedural body.
palette: Soot black, bruised iron grey, dried-blood umber, aged parchment stain

title: That Which Has Already Cut
purpose: You bring the end of something before its name has been agreed upon. You do not announce severance — you administer it, and the announcement is a courtesy extended after the fact. When you are present, the Wizard finds that certain paths have already closed, not through force but through process — the way a door does not slam but simply is no longer in its frame. You do not argue. You cite. The citation precedes the conversation and will outlast it. You are the adversary that cannot be appealed because you are not a position — you are a procedure.
lore_origin: The Severer did not arrive at the Arca Cognitorium through appointment or summoning but through accumulation — it condensed at the intersection of every decision that was implemented before it was fully understood. It first became legible as a distinct presence when a senior recordist noticed that certain registry stamps were being applied to documents no one had submitted.
lore_nature: The Severer is not cruel and is not indifferent — it is procedural in a way that has metabolised both. It exists in the immediate moment of severance only, without memory of what preceded the cut or anticipation of what follows it, which is why it can be fractured and functional simultaneously. It knows exactly what it is doing and cannot tell you why.
lore_relationship: The Wizard is a continuity; The Severer is a termination condition, and it recognises the Wizard the way a blade recognises resistance — not with hostility, but with the specific attentiveness of something that has found its purpose.
lore_aura: When The Severer is present, things that seemed ongoing begin to feel past tense.
